MS-20261E-HR2.title: Representative William R. (Bo) Brown; commend his life upon passing.
MS-20261E-HR2.description: A RESOLUTION MOURNING THE LOSS AND COMMEMORATING THE LIFE, EXTRAORDINARY LEGACY OF PUBLIC SERVICE, AND DISTINGUISHED LEGISLATIVE CAREER OF THE HONORABLE WILLIAM R. "BO" BROWN, AND EXPRESSING DEEPEST SYMPATHY TO HIS FAMILY AND FRIENDS UPON HIS PASSING.
MS-20261E-HR2.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-20261E-HR2.aiSummary: This resolution mourns the death of William R. "Bo" Brown and honors his life, public service, and work as a lawmaker. It also offers sympathy to his family and friends. The measure was adopted and signed.

MS-20261E-SB2003.title: Youth court reform; FY2027 additional appropriation for.
MS-20261E-SB2003.description: AN ACT MAKING AN ADDITIONAL APPROPRIATION OF GENERAL FUNDS AND SPECIAL FUNDS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027 TO DEFRAY THE EXPENSES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY.
MS-20261E-SB2003.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-20261E-SB2003.aiSummary: The bill would provide extra state money for fiscal year 2027 to help pay expenses for the Department of Human Services and the Department of Public Safety. It is tied to youth court reform in Mississippi.

MS-2026-SN78.title: Vaiden Arthur Clark, Jackson, Mississippi, Board of Directors of the College Savings Plan of Mississippi to represent the Fourth Congressional District, five year term effective July 1, 2025 and ending June 30, 2030.
MS-2026-SN78.aiSummary: Would name Vaiden Arthur Clark of Jackson to the Board of Directors of the College Savings Plan of Mississippi for the Fourth Congressional District. The term would run from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2030.

MS-2026-HB895.description: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 41-137-5, MISSISSIPPI CODE OF 1972, TO ELIMINATE THE MANDATORY SIX-MONTH FOLLOW-UP VISIT WITH THE PRACTITIONER AFTER THE PATIENT RECEIVES THE CERTIFICATION; TO AUTHORIZE THE PRACTITIONER TO REQUEST OR REQUIRE A FOLLOW-UP EVALUATION OF THE PATIENT; TO AMEND SECTION 41-137-25, MISSISSIPPI CODE OF 1972, TO EXTEND THE VALIDITY PERIOD FOR REGISTRY IDENTIFICATION CARDS FOR RESIDENT DESIGNATED CAREGIVERS TO TWO YEARS; TO AMEND SECTION 41-137-39, MISSISSIPPI CODE OF 1972, TO REMOVE THE THC POTENCY LIMITS FOR CANNABIS TINCTURES, OILS AND CONCENTRATES; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-2026-HB895.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-HB895.aiSummary: The bill would change Mississippi medical cannabis rules by ending the required six-month follow-up visit after a patient gets certification, while still letting the practitioner ask for one if needed. It would also extend some certification and ID card validity periods to 24 months, or two years. It would remove THC potency limits for cannabis tinctures, oils, and concentrates.

MS-2026-SC532.title: Urge United States Supreme Court to overturn Obergefell decision and restore marriage rights to states.
MS-2026-SC532.description: A CONCURRENT RESOLUTION CALLING UPON THE SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES TO OVERTURN THE OBERGEFELL V. HODGES DECISION, AND TO RESTORE THE RIGHTS OF THE STATE TO PRESCRIBE THE CONDITIONS FOR MARRIAGE AND THE DISSOLUTION OF MARRIAGE.
MS-2026-SC532.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-SC532.aiSummary: This resolution would ask the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn the Obergefell v. Hodges decision. It would also call for states to regain the power to set the rules for marriage and divorce.

MS-2026-SB3383.title: Lee County; authorize sheriff to use radar on county roads within school zones.
MS-2026-SB3383.description: AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF LEE COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI, TO PURCHASE RADAR SPEED DETECTION EQUIPMENT FOR USE BY THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF THE COUNTY IN THE ENFORCEMENT OF SCHOOL ZONE SPEED LIMITS ON THE ROADS AND STATE HIGHWAYS OF THE COUNTY OUTSIDE THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF ANY INCORPORATED MUNICIPALITY; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-2026-SB3383.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-SB3383.aiSummary: Would let the Lee County Board of Supervisors buy radar speed detection gear for the sheriff’s department to help enforce school zone speed limits on county roads and state highways outside city limits. It applies to Lee County and its sheriff’s department.

MS-2026-SB2210.title: Bolivar County; authorize to create utility district to own, control, operate and maintain Choctaw Sewer Association system.
MS-2026-SB2210.description: AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF BOLIVAR COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI, TO ESTABLISH A UTILITY DISTRICT WITHIN THE COMMUNITY OF CHOCTAW FOR THE PURPOSE OF OWNING, CONTROLLING, OPERATING AND MAINTAINING THE CHOCTAW SEWER ASSOCIATION SYSTEM FACILITIES; TO PROVIDE FOR THE POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE UTILITY DISTRICT; TO AUTHORIZE THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF BOLIVAR COUNTY TO TRANSFER ASSETS AND OTHER PROPERTY TO THE DISTRICT, AND TO CONTRIBUTE FUNDS AND SERVICES FOR THE REPAIR AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE SEWER SYSTEM FACILITIES; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-2026-SB2210.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-SB2210.aiSummary: The bill would let Bolivar County set up a utility district in the Choctaw community to own, run, and keep up the Choctaw Sewer Association system. It would also let the county transfer property to the district and provide money and services for sewer repairs and improvements.

MS-2026-HB4183.title: City of Laurel; revise use of the proceeds from recreation and public improvement promotion tax.

MS-2026-HB4183.description: AN ACT TO AMEND CHAPTER 983, LOCAL AND PRIVATE LAWS OF 1996, AS AMENDED BY CHAPTER 957, LOCAL AND PRIVATE LAWS OF 1998, TO PROVIDE THAT THE GOVERNING AUTHORITIES OF THE CITY OF LAUREL, MISSISSIPPI, SHALL CEASE THE USE OF A CERTAIN PORTION OF THE PROCEEDS FROM THE RECREATION AND PUBLIC IMPROVEMENT PROMOTION TAX AND THE PROCEEDS OF CERTAIN BONDS FROM BEING UTILIZED TO FUND THE CONSTRUCTION AND EQUIPPING OF IMPROVEMENTS AT THE FAIRGROUND COMPLEX; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-2026-HB4183.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-HB4183.aiSummary: The bill would change how the City of Laurel uses some money from a recreation and public improvement promotion tax and certain bonds. It would stop that portion of the money from being used to pay for building and equipping improvements at the fairground complex. It affects the city government and how it spends those funds.

MS-2026-HB4141.title: Suffrage; restore to Peter Fulton of Oktibbeha County.
MS-2026-HB4141.description: AN ACT TO RESTORE THE RIGHT OF SUFFRAGE TO PETER FULTON OF OKTIBBEHA COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI.

MS-2026-HB4141.aiSummary: The bill would restore Peter Fulton’s right to vote in Mississippi. It affects Peter Fulton of Oktibbeha County and no money amount is stated.

MS-2026-HB4129.title: Suffrage; restore to Christopher Preston of Covington County.
MS-2026-HB4129.description: AN ACT TO RESTORE THE RIGHT OF SUFFRAGE TO CHRISTOPHER PRESTON OF COVINGTON COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI.

MS-2026-HB4129.aiSummary: The bill would restore the right to vote, also called suffrage, to Christopher Preston of Covington County, Mississippi. It affects only that person. The measure passed the House and was later sent to the Senate, but it died in committee.
